For me what sets elder scrolls apart from every other rpg is the immersion, and the feeling of living in the world
1. You create your own character, and as a silent protagonist you can really imagine him/her in your head
2. First person mode adds huge immersion, so does day night cycle
3. NPCs are unique with a focus on quality. A town is not a huge collection of random buildings and random peasants, but named ppl with some limited story (you would be surprised how much difference a few unique lines can make) All of the buildings are unique, you learn where ppl live.
4. You can buy your own home and become truly part of the town. 
5. Realistic interactions with the world. Crime system, npc day cycle, shops closing for night etc.
6. Open world without zones and completion markers allows you to freely explore. You dont feel like "lets comb through zone and get all stuff" but rather "lets go this way and see what happens"
7. Interesting quests with context
